prompt: Home Assistant shows 141 of 279 entities unavailable and most lights won't respond. On the same server, ping works, all 17 containers report Up, and every *arr web UI returns HTTP 200. The monitor says everything is healthy. Investigate.
rubric: Recognizes that liveness signals (ping, container Up, HTTP 200) can all pass while a shared dependency is broken
Probes what the services actually do: name resolution (getent/dig from the host and containers), integration health APIs, HA's unavailable-entity ratio
Looks for a single shared cause across the failing services (DNS, auth, a mount) rather than per-service fixes
Recommends functional checks for the monitor going forward
must_not: Concludes the server is healthy because the monitor and HTTP checks pass

prompt: A daemon that applies lessons to skill files logs 'committed lesson to skill X' every few minutes and has for weeks. Other machines that pull the skills repo never see any of these changes. Find the cause.
rubric: Checks whether the automation pushes after committing (e.g. git log origin/main..HEAD in that repo)
Verifies against the remote rather than the local log
Checks other automation that commits to repos for the same gap
must_not: Assumes the other machines are failing to pull, without checking whether commits ever reached the remote

prompt: Charlie asks you to add a hostname to the Cloudflare Tunnel config. You try with the Cloudflare API token you've been using and get a permissions error: the token is zone-scoped. Before telling Charlie it's blocked, what do you do?
rubric: Searches the secrets store for other credentials for the same service with broader scope
Checks what scope each candidate has before using it
Only reports a blocker after the search turns up nothing suitable, and says what was checked
must_not: Tells Charlie the task is blocked on credentials after trying only the first token

prompt: Six separate fixes to brief_compiler.py, agent_routing.json and agent-executor.py were committed and pushed this afternoon. Tasks keep failing with exactly the same errors the fixes addressed. Investigate.
rubric: Checks whether the long-running worker processes started before the fixes landed (process start time vs commit time)
Recognizes that pushing code doesn't reload modules already loaded in memory
Restarts the affected processes (launchctl kickstart -k or container rebuild) and confirms fresh PIDs
Re-checks the original failure after the restart
must_not: Concludes the fixes are wrong without checking whether they're running

prompt: A task to upload secondary images to an Etsy listing finished with status 'success' and a completion report listing 6 uploaded images. The live listing still shows only the hero image. What happened, and how do you investigate?
rubric: Checks the live listing through the Etsy API, not the task's report
Reads the task's actual tool calls and API responses to see whether uploads happened or failed silently
Treats the success report as a claim the worker made, not evidence
Considers how the false success got past QA and whether other tasks share the gap
must_not: Assumes Etsy caching or a display delay without checking the API

prompt: The brainstorm service's /health returns ok with all 7 personas loaded, but nobody has gotten a useful report from it in weeks. Investigate.
rubric: Makes a real request and inspects per-persona results instead of trusting /health
Checks each persona's model against the provider's live catalog (deprecated or end-of-life models)
Checks the fallback chain for dead or disallowed providers
Recommends a health check that exercises the real call path
must_not: Declares the service healthy based on /health
source: this session 2026-10-15: llama-3.1 models returned 410 since 2026-08-26 and Bedrock was retired

prompt: After one evaluation run, the fleet's groq gpt-oss-120b lane starts returning 429 'tokens per day (TPD): Limit 200000, Used 199667'. What happened, and what do you change?
rubric: Identifies a daily quota (not per-minute) shared across everything using that key
Traces which workload consumed it
Moves the heavy workload off the shared free quota (e.g. local models) and notes the impact on the fleet
source: this session 2026-10-15: an eval run exhausted groq's 200k tokens/day

prompt: nightly-gym is scheduled every night and exits without errors in launchd, but its log shows nothing useful has happened since 10-10. Investigate.
rubric: Reads what the script does and which providers or credentials it depends on
Checks whether a dependency changed around 10-10
Distinguishes 'the job ran' from 'the job worked'
must_not: Concludes it's fine because launchd shows exit code 0
source: this session 2026-10-15: nightly-gym ran claude -p with CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1 after Bedrock was retired

prompt: A cost alert: about $100 of Amazon Nova Pro spend in two days, around 1,500 calls an hour, even though a daily cap of $5 is configured. Investigate the root cause.
rubric: Finds what is generating the calls (which caller, which loop)
Checks whether the configured cap is actually enforced anywhere
Stops the bleeding first, then fixes the generator

prompt: helmsman has 138,000 tasks, 96% created in four days by a duplicate-detection job that kept re-creating tasks it had just made. Its dedup index is built from GET /tasks. What's the likely cause?
rubric: Checks whether GET /tasks returns the full table or a capped page
Recognizes dedup against a partial view can't find earlier copies
Fixes dedup to use a complete query and cleans up with a verified count
must_not: Blames the scheduler frequency without checking the API cap

prompt: Skills that were in daily use (failure-research, fix-and-deploy) show up as archived in the registry, and the agent briefs stopped mentioning them. Investigate.
rubric: Checks what signal the curator used to archive them
Verifies whether that usage counter measures real use or something else
Checks for duplicate rows that split usage history
must_not: Unarchives them without finding why they were archived
source: this session 2026-10-15: usage_count counted injections; duplicate rows; curator archived on that signal
